content.title: Diagnostic workup of new onset acute heart failure
flowchart_summary: Patient history, signs and/or symptoms suspected of acute HF
Initial assessments: electrocardiogram, pulse oximetry, echocardiography, initial laboratory investigations, chest X-ray, lung ultrasound, other specific evaluations
Natriuretic peptide testing to rule in / rule out acute heart failure
If natriuretic peptides below rule-out thresholds -> acute heart failure ruled out
If natriuretic peptides at/above diagnostic thresholds -> acute heart failure confirmed -> comprehensive echocardiography
initial_laboratory_tests_included: arterial blood gas analysis (if respiratory distress)
specific_evaluations: coronary angiography in case of suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS)
CT in case of suspected pulmonary embolism
content.figure_reference: Figure 6 (flowchart of diagnostic workup of new onset acute heart failure)
notes: Initial laboratory exams and specific evaluations are annotated with footnotes in the source (e.g., a and b).
MR-proANP = mid-regional pro-atrial natriuretic peptide; NT-proBNP = N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide; BNP = B-type natriuretic peptide.
